subject.title: [improvement] Sub-agent cascade circuit breaker for multi-agent team reliability

question: Should OpenClaw core add a first-class subagent cascade breaker, and what scope, default behavior, persistence model, and operator recovery surface should it own?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the permanent behavior crosses config schema, runtime admission, persisted state, failure taxonomy, notification, UI/CLI status, and overlap with broader session/tool/provider guard work.

options.title: Design a first-class subagent breaker
options.body: Define the scoped failure receipt, thresholds, cooldown or half-open behavior, reset/override semantics, and operator-visible state before implementation.

options.title: Fold into broader session-health work
options.body: Treat this as a subagent-specific requirement under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62615 and implement one shared health contract later.

options.title: Defer to narrower guards
options.body: Keep existing timeout, active-child, provider cooldown, and tool-loop guards separate and close or narrow this request only after an explicit maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Design a first-class subagent breaker
recommendation.body: Define the scoped failure receipt, thresholds, cooldown or half-open behavior, reset/override semantics, and operator-visible state before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the broadest recent history across the subagent spawn, registry, and control-boundary surfaces that this contract would need to coordinate.
